title: Rav Papa Saba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He always spoke in the name of Rav, as in Kiddushin 71b, Sanhedrin 49b, Menachot 33b.

Yuchasin, under Daor bar Papa, lists eleven sons of Rav Papa Saba who lived in Rav’s time. Its author writes that he heard from his father, who received the tradition from elder sages, that their names help against forgetfulness.

Sefer HaEshkol, Laws of Torah Scrolls, says that the eleven sons of Rav Papa were not all sons of one Rav Papa but lived at different times. It too preserves a tradition that their names help remove forgetfulness, and mentions the custom of reciting them at the completion of a tractate.

notes.text: The tradition concerns reciting the names to counter forgetfulness. Hyman preserves both an eleven-sons list and Sefer HaEshkol’s warning that they lived at different times and had different fathers.

Kiddushin 71b directly names Rav Papa Saba reporting Rav. The universal always statement, Yuchasin’s eleven-sons list and Sefer HaEshkol’s different-fathers-and-eras account remain Hyman’s reports; their exact editions have not been independently inspected here.
